entry_conditions: Drawer is open and stable, block remains low in a valid tunnel pose, current TCP/configuration is finite and collision-free, gripper is open unless restarting after a plausible grasp, and two causal frames persist across the policy switch.
exit_conditions: Closed fingers remain near the block, object and TCP show coupled motion, object is outside the tunnel above world z 0.16 m, and local body-frame corrections have turned toward the drawer destination.
overlap_role: The complete 300:840 segment is supervised. Actions 300:440 teach continuation from predecessor retreat/approach; 680:840 teach clearance, reorientation and transfer shared with placement.
successor_readiness: Switch in the shared tail after persistent observed object/TCP coupling, clearance above 0.16 m and destination-directed motion. A closed command by itself is not sufficient.
failure_signatures: Local corrections drift away from object or destination, object fails to follow closed fingers, phase oscillates near closure/lift, object remains low, or IK repeatedly reports nonconvergence or limits.
continuation_guidance: Resolve every action against the fresh TCP rather than accumulating predicted deltas. Prefer h01 if reliable block displacement is the principal variation; prefer h03 if premature low transfer is the dominant concern.
limitations: The successful demonstrations do not show unusual handoffs or recovery, so handoff robustness is expected rather than established. No contact truth, collision checker or failed-grasp retry is available.
